original_question: Asymptotically evaluate each of the following additive-divisor correlations: sum_{n<=x} d3(n) d3(n+1); sum_{n<=x} d(n) d(n+1) d(n+2); for every kappa in (0,1), sum_{n<=x} d_kappa(n) d(n+1) d(n+2); and for every kappa in (2,3), sum_{n<=x} d_kappa(n) d3(n+1).
target_in_paper: Section "Additive divisor sums/shifted convolution sums", Problem (27): the four additive-divisor-sum asymptotic evaluation problems listed there.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's actual target extremely closely: it identifies the correct open problem, includes all four sums in Problem (27), keeps the exact shifts n+1 and n+2, and preserves the two parameter ranges kappa in (0,1) and kappa in (2,3).
missing_details: Define the generalized divisor function d_alpha(n): for alpha>0, zeta(s)^alpha = sum_{n=1}^infinity d_alpha(n)n^{-s} for Re(s)>1.
Make explicit that d(n)=d_2(n) is the ordinary divisor function, and d_3(n) is the 3-fold divisor function.
Specify that the summation variable n runs over positive integers.
Specify that x is a positive real parameter and the asymptotic is sought as x -> infinity.
State that kappa is a fixed real parameter in the indicated interval for each of the last two sums.
Clarify that the paper asks for asymptotic formulae, but does not itself prescribe a particular main-term shape or error term; a faithful rewrite should not add one.
Identify the exact source as Problem (27) in the section on additive divisor sums/shifted convolution sums; this is an open problem, not a theorem or conjecture elsewhere in the paper.
refined_question: Let d_alpha(n) denote the generalized divisor function defined for alpha>0 by zeta(s)^alpha = sum_{n=1}^infinity d_alpha(n)n^{-s} for Re(s)>1, so that d(n)=d_2(n). As x -> infinity, obtain asymptotic formulae for each of the following additive divisor sums over positive integers n: sum_{n<=x} d_3(n)d_3(n+1); sum_{n<=x} d(n)d(n+1)d(n+2); for each fixed real kappa in (0,1), sum_{n<=x} d_kappa(n)d(n+1)d(n+2); and for each fixed real kappa in (2,3), sum_{n<=x} d_kappa(n)d_3(n+1).
justification: This is exactly Problem (27) in the paper's additive-divisor-sums section. The draft is already very close to the official formulation; the only needed refinements are the notation needed to make it stand-alone, namely the definition of d_alpha(n), the identification d(n)=d_2(n), the fact that n ranges over positive integers, that x tends to infinity, and that kappa is fixed real in the stated intervals. The paper gives no alternate equivalent reformulation and does not specify a conjectural main-term template here, so a faithful rewrite should not add either.
